content.text:
<pasted_content id="7326">
Connect Understand and Test into one flow. Presentation and read-only API only: no worker changes, no new SQL unless unavoidable (test runs already store brief_run_id). Keep it within 20 minutes. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Do not read or print any env file. Do not commit.

1. Report → brief: when a test run has brief_run_id, show at the top of the report "From your brief of {site} ← Back to brief", and after the findings a "Test another journey" block listing the brief's suggested journeys not yet tested, each with "Test this journey".
2. Brief → progress: on each suggested journey card, if a test run from this brief used that goal, show its status (Running, Got through, Stuck, and so on, using the verdict colours) and link to its report. Add a read-only API that lists runs where brief_run_id = the brief id (id, goal, status, verdict kind only).
3. Returning visitor: on the home page, a small "Your recent runs" list of the last 10 briefs and reports started from this browser (site, type, status chip, time, link). Store only run ids, kinds, site names and times in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch; never goals with personal data, never logins. Include a "Clear" link. Hide the section when empty.
4. Keep the test form draft (goal, success condition, way in, but never test login fields) in sessionStorage so a reload doesn't lose it.
Check at 390 px and 1280 px using brief 8ca3896f-a3d8-475f-b810-5c9b6b98bb9e. Run web tests, typecheck, lint and build.
</pasted_content id="7326">

content.text:
All four parts are in. Tests (66 passing, including a new test file), typecheck, lint and build all pass. Nothing is committed, the worker and SQL are untouched, and I didn't read any env file.

**What I added**
1. **Report → brief:** when a test came from a brief, the report now starts with "From your brief of plausible.io ← Back to brief". After the findings there's a "Test another journey" block. It lists the brief's suggested journeys that no test has used yet, each with its own "Test this journey" button. If every journey has been tested, it says so and links back to the brief. To make this work, the report's existing API now also returns `brief_run_id`, with the same fallback the other newer columns use for older databases.
2. **Brief → progress:** each journey card shows the newest test that used its goal (Running, Got through, Stuck and so on, in the verdict colours) with a link to it. The card's button then reads "Test it again". The new read-only API is `GET /api/briefs/[id]/runs` and returns only `id, goal, status, verdict_kind`. It lists only test runs, because founder briefs also use `brief_run_id`. Goals count as the same journey if they differ only in case, spacing or a final full stop.
3. **Your recent runs:** a list on the home page, just below the form. Each row shows the site, Brief or Test, a status chip, how long ago, and a link. localStorage holds only the id, kind, host name and start time. Only the host is kept, so a path, query or `user:password` typed into the address never gets stored. Storage access is wrapped in try/catch, there's a "Clear" link, and the list is hidden when empty.
4. **Form draft:** goal, success condition and the chosen way in are kept in sessionStorage. The draft is cleared once a test starts, and it doesn't overwrite a form filled in from a brief's link.

**Decisions to check**
- **Extra API:** the home list needs each run's status, so I added a second small read-only route, `GET /api/runs/status?ids=…`. It takes at most 10 ids and returns only `id, kind, status, verdict_kind`. Without it, the page would have to load each full report.
- **Start link not saved:** I read "way in" as the access choice only. The start-link text isn't kept because it can contain a guest token. The login fields aren't kept either.
- **Moved colours:** the verdict colours moved from `report-v2.tsx` into `lib/verdict-look.ts` so the brief and home page can share them; the report still exports them under the old name. On the small chips I used the hero's verdict colours: the hero's dark chip colours were almost invisible in dark mode.

**Visual check:** I took screenshots of the brief 8ca3896f…, a report, and the home page at 390 px and 1280 px, using headless Chrome against a local production build. No page scrolls sideways. The saved draft came back after a reload, and "Clear" emptied storage and hid the list. No test has been started from this brief yet, so the API correctly returns an empty list. To see the chips and the report links, my screenshot script faked two responses inside the browser only: it attached this brief to an existing report and pretended the brief had one running test and one stuck one. Nothing was written to the database. The blinking "Running" dot stops under prefers-reduced-motion through the existing rule in `tokens.css`.
